Irish authorities, including Garda, customs, and the Health Products Regulatory Authority, seized over 60,000 vials of anabolic steroids, human growth hormones, and erectile dysfunction pills during raids in Muff and Lifford. While a man in his 30s was arrested, he was subsequently released without charge, though officials confirmed evidence of an illegal manufacturing operation. Further searches were also conducted by the PSNI in Northern Ireland as part of the investigation.

DUP MP Ian Paisley dismissed Taoiseach Enda Kenny’s suggestion that Brexit could trigger a referendum on Irish unity as "mischievous," arguing that such a vote is unlikely to occur. While Sinn Féin’s Gerry Adams welcomed the comments as creating a greater opportunity for a united Ireland, other unionist politicians, including Paisley and Jenny Palmer, maintained that a border poll is not feasible and urged a focus on economic stability instead.

Morecambe manager Danny Bentley has urged his team to stay grounded despite their recent success, which includes knocking out Championship side Rotherham and winning three consecutive league games to top the table. Bentley praised 37-year-old Kevin Ellison for his professionalism and leadership, highlighting how his attitude positively influences the squad. The manager emphasized the importance of maintaining balance and unity, regardless of whether the team is experiencing a winning streak or a difficult spell.

Qatar’s foreign minister has rejected a list of 13 demands imposed by Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the UAE, and Bahrain, arguing that the conditions infringe on Qatar's sovereignty rather than addressing terrorism. While the blockading nations have set a 10-day deadline to close media outlets and reduce ties with Iran, US Secretary of State Rex Tillerson described the proposals as a basis for dialogue and urged all parties to lower their rhetoric to resolve the crisis. Meanwhile, Qatar continues to withstand economic sanctions through alternative supply routes, even as its citizens face expulsion orders from neighboring countries.

Natalie Evans, who is currently suspended from UKIP, has announced she will not run for the party leadership, claiming that senior figures have manipulated party rules to block her candidacy. Instead, she has endorsed councillor Lisa Duffy as the best candidate to succeed Nigel Farage and steer the party toward a more moderate, "common sense centre-ground." Evans maintains that her suspension was politically motivated and argued that the party needs significant internal reform to shed its hard-right image.

A Delhi court has charged an Uber driver with rape and criminal intimidation after a woman reported being assaulted during a ride, leading authorities to ban Uber and other ride-hailing services for inadequate safety checks. While police state the driver has confessed, this incident highlights the ongoing crisis of sexual violence in India, which has persisted despite stricter laws enacted following the high-profile 2012 Delhi gang-rape case. Recent arrests in other cities further underscore the failure of current measures to deter such crimes against women.

Wales' historic Euro 2016 campaign ended in the semi-finals with a loss to Portugal, yet the atmosphere remained celebratory due to the profound bond between the team and their passionate supporters. This symbiotic relationship has transformed the national experience, turning a 58-year absence from major tournaments into a dreamlike era of success and widespread joy across Wales. The squad’s achievements have not only broken psychological barriers but also created a lasting legacy of mutual adoration between the players and the nation.

Glasgow has once again dominated the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation, accounting for 56 of the 100 most deprived areas, although this represents a slight improvement from the previous year. While local councils argue that their innovative long-term strategies are beginning to make a difference, the Scottish government and opposition parties emphasize that deep-seated poverty requires sustained political action and greater devolved powers to address systemic inequalities. The report highlights the ongoing challenge of tackling deprivation amidst welfare cuts and austerity measures, with calls for a new approach to regenerate local economies.

British rowers Cassells and Scrimgeour secured their spot in the lightweight pairs final with the fastest qualifying time, defending their title from last year. Meanwhile, Irish Olympic silver medallist Paul O'Donovan advanced to the lightweight single sculls final after winning his semi-final, and his brother Mark O'Donovan along with partner Shane O'Driscol also qualified for the lightweight pairs final. The Rotterdam championships features both Olympic and non-Olympic classes, with finals scheduled for Saturday.

Scottish Championship club Raith Rovers have signed 22-year-old Johnston, along with defenders Craig Barr and striker Mark Stewart, on one-year contracts. Johnston, who previously played for Kilmarnock and Fife-based Raith Rovers, joins Barr and Stewart, who both spent the last season with the club before its relegation to League One. The trio represents a significant recruitment effort for the team as they look to rebuild following their drop in division.

Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory over Swansea City, with James Milner scoring the late winner to extend their winning streak to four Premier League games. Although Swansea’s spirited first-half performance, which saw Leroy Fer open the scoring, bought manager Francesco Guidolin some time, their inability to hold off Liverpool’s dominant second-half display leaves his future at the club uncertain. The result highlights Liverpool's recent attacking form while underscoring Swansea's ongoing struggles, as they remain just one point above the relegation zone.

Sam Chalmers has become the first Scottish rugby player to receive a positive steroids test, admitting he obtained the substances online despite claiming he was sorry. The article argues that while physical pressure to gain size is real, purchasing performance-enhancing drugs constitutes cheating, noting that approximately 1.4% of elite rugby players globally have been caught violating anti-doping rules. It further suggests that the normalization of supplements in youth rugby may be creating a slippery slope toward the use of illegal steroids.

TRNSMT, Scotland's newest music festival, is launching at Glasgow Green this weekend, headlined by Radiohead, Kasabian, and Biffy Clyro, as a replacement for the suspended T in the Park. Organizers DF Concerts introduced the event following a challenging period for T in the Park, which faced severe criticism over safety issues and logistical failures in previous years. In response to recent terror attacks, police have implemented strict security measures, including armed patrols and a zero-tolerance policy on drugs and pyrotechnics.

North Korea has officially confirmed the restart of its Yongbyon nuclear reactor, a move that violates previous disarmament agreements and has drawn strong criticism from the White House. US officials have urged Pyongyang to fulfill its international obligations and refrain from provocative actions, emphasizing that the international community will not accept North Korea as a nuclear state. This development escalates regional tensions and stalls the six-party talks aimed at ending North Korea's nuclear program, which have been inactive since 2009.

Cambridshire Police have arrested a 64-year-old man after human bones consistent with being Andrew Bedford were discovered during a reopened murder investigation into his 1990 disappearance. Bedford, who was last seen in Ramsey in September 1990, is believed to have been shot, and the recovered remains are now undergoing DNA testing and forensic analysis. Detectives remain confident that local information will help bring resolution to the case, which has remained unsolved for over three decades.

Salford City Reds owner Dr. Marwan Koukash is aggressively pursuing a vision to transform the struggling club into the country's largest rugby team, leveraging his wealth to attract high-profile figures like coach Brian Noble and player Adrian Morley. Central to this ambitious project is Koukash's campaign to raise the Super League's salary cap, arguing that increased spending is necessary to compete for top talent and reverse the sport's financial decline. While the initiative has generated significant enthusiasm and discussion within the rugby community, the final outcome remains uncertain as key figures weigh the financial risks against the potential for growth.

Ireland secured their third consecutive victory in the qualifying tournament by defeating Zimbabwe, thanks to Isobel Joyce’s four wickets and Cecilia Joyce’s top score of 36. This win keeps Ireland's hopes alive for a spot in next year's World Twenty20, with a final match against Scotland determining their fate. The top two teams from this qualifying group will advance to compete against the world's elite in India.

Colchester Hospital has been rated as inadequate by the Care Quality Commission due to its reliance on "unsuitable" agency staff and poor leadership, prompting a recommendation that it remain in special measures for another three months. The report has reignited anger from the family of Norman Betchley, who died in 2009 due to a mistake by an agency nurse, as they feel the same systemic failures persist. Hospital chief executive Frank Sims has acknowledged the critical issue of agency dependency and pledged to focus entirely on improving the trust's standing this year.

Mark Cavendish sits third in the overall points standings after finishing sixth in the scratch race and seventh in the elimination race, while Becky James broke the women's sprint Olympic record to advance to the quarter-finals. Cavendish’s teammate, Elia Viviani, leads the competition with 106 points, followed by Cavendish on 96, as the field prepares for the time trial and remaining events on Monday. Meanwhile, James and fellow Briton Katy Marchant have both secured their spots in the quarter-finals, with James setting a new Olympic record during qualification.

Finance Minister Máirtín Ó Muilleoir announced a reallocation of funds that adds an additional £200m to the health budget for 2016/17, addressing urgent needs identified by Health Minister Michelle O'Neill. While specific details are still being finalized, the funding is expected to prioritize unscheduled care and resolve bed-blocking issues in hospitals. The reallocation also includes significant investments in schools, road maintenance, and further education, funded in part by savings from reversed tax credit cuts.

Days after withdrawing a Supreme Court appeal, the Winklevoss twins have filed a new lawsuit against Facebook, alleging that Mark Zuckerberg intentionally suppressed evidence during previous settlement proceedings. The suit claims that crucial documents regarding the relationship between Zuckerberg and the twins were withheld, despite the parties having already reached a $65 million settlement in 2008. Facebook’s legal team has dismissed these claims as baseless and previously rejected by the courts.

South Yorkshire Police are appealing for witnesses after a teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus in Thrybergh, Rotherham, on Saturday. The driver of the vehicle was not injured in the incident, which occurred as the car was traveling towards Dalton. Authorities are urging anyone with information about the crash to come forward.

Harry Chapman Pincher was a prominent Daily Express defence correspondent renowned for his exceptional memory and unorthodox investigative methods, which often involved securing scoops through informal lunches and countryside meetings. After retiring, he published books alleging that Britain's security services had been penetrated by high-level spies, while also revealing that MI5 had been monitoring his conversations without taking action. His career was defined by his ability to bypass official channels to expose sensitive information about Britain's atomic weapons programme and political affairs.

Dundee striker Ryan Stewart has agreed to personal terms and passed his medical to join Birmingham City, reversing his previous rejection of a move to the club. The 23-year-old, who has scored six goals in three games this season, could make his debut in Saturday's Championship match against Leeds. Stewart becomes Birmingham's second signing of the week, following the arrival of Che Adams, as the club looks to bounce back from a poor start to their season.

A former private in her 20s has accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office as part of the Metropolitan Police's Operation Elveden. She agreed to pay £40 to an armed forces charity, a decision made by the Crown Prosecution Service after determining that prosecution was not in the public interest despite sufficient evidence. This case marks the 87th arrest under the inquiry, which investigates corrupt payments to public officials following the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.

The Care Inspectorate has issued severe warnings to two Glasgow care homes, Nithsdale House and Drumpellier Lodge, following unannounced inspections in February that revealed significant failures in care quality, staffing, and management. Nithsdale House received the lowest possible rating of one across three key areas, while Drumpellier Lodge was rated as "weak" in similar categories, with both facilities failing to address previous improvement requirements. The Inspectorate has stated that unless these providers demonstrate significant and urgent improvements, they will not hesitate to take further regulatory action.

Metropolitan Police officers arrested four men in Enfield on Saturday afternoon after receiving reports of a gun being seen in a vehicle. The suspects were apprehended when their car was stopped at 16:00 GMT and are currently being held at a north London police station.

A power outage at Lancaster's Caton Road substation left 53,000 properties without electricity, causing significant disruptions to travel, schools, and local businesses. Power was fully restored by 16:30 BST, though the cause of the failure remains unknown. The incident forced the closure of several key facilities, including Lancaster Town Hall and Salt Ayre Leisure Centre, while universities and other institutions managed the crisis with limited resources.

High Court Judge Mr Justice Gilbart has quashed Local Government Secretary Sajiv Javid’s refusal to approve the Hatchfield Farm development in Newmarket, ruling that the decision was inconsistent and failed to apply national planning policies. The judge determined that the area requires more land for housing and economic growth, thereby invalidating the previous rejection. The case will now be reconsidered by the Secretary of State, who must now account for the significant benefits the development would bring to the town.

Following a series of operational failures including breakdowns, groundings, and vehicle damage, the council has ordered an audit of the new Cowes chain ferry and waived crossing fees until July 2 to gather feedback. While local business owners are demanding compensation for significant trade losses, council officials describe the issues as "teething problems" in a prototype project that have largely been rectified. The council is currently discussing potential compensation for affected businesses alongside the implementation of technical fixes like ramp extensions.

Tunisia international Sliti has signed a permanent three-year contract with Lille, converting his previous season-long loan into a full-time deal. The 24-year-old midfielder, who has made 16 appearances for the club and earned 11 caps for his country, joins the team as they sit 11th in the league table.

British astronaut Tim Peake, who has been in space for six weeks, took time to engage with children by sharing experiments and speaking directly with them. Leah met with some of the students who were fortunate enough to have this direct interaction with the astronaut.

Martyn Irvine has been named BBC Northern Ireland's Sports Personality of the Year after becoming the first Irish cyclist to win a world track title in 117 years. Despite suffering a fractured hip earlier in the year, Irvine recovered to secure a world gold and silver medal, along with other international successes, beating runners-up AP McCoy and Michael Dunlop for the award.

An Italian C-27J aircraft lost communication while flying from Iceland to Italy, prompting RAF Typhoons to intercept and escort it to Prestwick Airport as a precautionary measure. The plane landed safely without incident, causing only minor delays to other flights, while local police took over the situation after the military aircraft departed.

Five men were arrested in Birmingham and Stoke-on-Trent on suspicion of terrorism after bomb disposal officers cordoned off Birmingham's Lee Bank area to deal with two suspect devices. Magistrates have granted police a further seven days to question the suspects as the West Midlands Counter Terrorism Unit continues its intelligence-led investigation.

The UEFA European Championship kicks off on June 10 with an expanded field of 24 teams, marking the first time the tournament features six groups and a modified knockout format. Favorites include defending champions Spain, World Cup winners Germany, and host nation France, who are favored by bookmakers despite missing key striker Karim Benzema. The tournament highlights include the debut of Wales and Northern Ireland, as well as a high-profile group stage clash between England and Wales.

Great Britain will host Greece at the Copper Box in London for their only home game before the FIBA EuroBasket 2017, offering the team a chance for revenge after a recent defeat in Patras. The match, which will be broadcast on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website, features key players like Teddy Okereafor who view the event as crucial preparation for the upcoming tournament. Following this fixture, GB coach Joe Prunty’s squad will travel to Poland for their final warm-up games before EuroBasket begins in September.

Australia secured a narrow victory over Wales in a tightly contested match, largely thanks to Bernard Foley’s kicking and a heroic defensive effort that held firm during a critical seven-minute period when the Wallabies played with 13 men. Despite having numerical superiority, Wales failed to capitalize on their advantage, resulting in their 11th consecutive defeat against Australia and extending a losing streak that dates back to 2008. The win sends Australia through to face Scotland in the quarter-finals, while Wales must now prepare for a challenging match against South Africa.

Scotland captain Greig Laidlaw has urged his team to deliver a strong performance for outgoing coach Vern Cotter as they face Ireland in the Six Nations opener. Despite Scotland's poor historical record against Ireland and the threat posed by Ireland's tactically astute coach Joe Schmidt, the Scots are motivated to provide a fitting farewell for their departing coach. Meanwhile, Ireland captain Rory Best anticipates a challenging set-piece battle against Scotland's inexperienced front row, though he acknowledges their individual club form.

Retired General David Petraeus argues that defeating the Islamic State requires a strategy combining military force with political solutions, warning that "industrial-strength" extremists cannot be defeated by arms alone. He characterizes IS as a formidable conventional army with insurgent and terrorist elements, noting that their recent capture of Ramadi represents a significant strategic setback that necessitates a review of current tactics. Petraeus emphasizes that long-term success depends on providing political incentives for Sunni Arabs to support the Iraqi government rather than oppose it.

The City of Edinburgh Council confirmed that a cyber attack on its website service provider resulted in the exposure of only email addresses, with no other personal data compromised. Officials have reported the incident to the Information Commissioner and the UK Government's Computer Emergency Response Team, while warning affected individuals about potential spam or phishing emails. The council stated that the breach was handled swiftly and that no council services were disrupted during the incident.

Syrian rebel groups have launched a major offensive against government forces in Latakia and Hama, accusing regime troops of violating the US-Russia-brokered ceasefire by targeting residential areas and displaced people. In response to this escalation, the Syrian opposition delegation in Geneva announced its intention to suspend formal peace talks, citing the collapse of the cessation of hostilities and accusing the UN envoy of bias. Despite the threat of walking out, opposition delegates remain in Geneva for informal discussions, while the US urges Russia to use its influence to halt the attacks and preserve the fragile diplomatic process.

Instagram is launching its first advertising program in a few months, marking a significant step toward building a sustainable business model after being acquired by Facebook for $1 billion. The company has clarified that users retain ownership of their photos, aiming to address previous backlash regarding privacy concerns while capitalizing on the booming social media advertising market. This move aligns with Facebook's broader strategy to increase its share of global mobile ad revenues, which is projected to rise significantly this year.

Dexter star Cillian Murphy is set to perform David Bowie’s title track from the album *Blackstar* at the upcoming Mercury Music Prize ceremony. The event, scheduled for September 15, will see Radiohead and other nominees compete for the £25,000 prize, with the final winner determined by a panel of judges after a public vote narrows the field to six finalists.

Retired detective Gurpal Virdi was acquitted of indecently assaulting a male prisoner and misconduct in public office at Southwark Crown Court. The charges, which dated back to 1986, were part of a long-standing dispute that Virdi claimed was a 17-year campaign by the Metropolitan Police to discredit him following his testimony on racism within the force. Virdi, who retired in 2012 after 30 years of service, maintained that the prosecution was an attempt to "hound" him out of the police.

Following the recent election, UK government ministers are facing pressure to adopt a more flexible Brexit approach that maintains close ties with the EU single market to achieve cross-party consensus. While some politicians argue for remaining in the single market to ensure frictionless trade, others maintain that staying in it would contradict the clear mandate to leave, emphasizing the need for a deal that balances sovereignty with economic access. The government has begun consulting with devolved administrations, acknowledging their increased importance in shaping the final outcome of the negotiations.

Following the Hillsborough inquests, Home Secretary Theresa May held private meetings with victims' families, who urged her to implement a "Hillsborough Law" to ensure public officials cooperate with investigations and to address the conduct of South Yorkshire Police. While the families welcomed the jury's finding of unlawful killing, they expressed frustration over the police's behavior during the inquests and demanded assurances regarding potential criminal prosecutions. Meanwhile, the Independent Police Complaints Commission continues its historic inquiry, having gathered statements from 168 officers and preparing to submit evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service by year-end.

The Crown Prosecution Service has issued new guidance stating that online harassment, including virtual mobbing and doxxing, will be prosecuted with the same severity as offline offenses. Director of Public Prosecutions Alison Saunders emphasized that while the internet is not a consequence-free zone, prosecutors will exercise caution to ensure that legitimate free speech is not stifled. This policy shift aims to help police identify online crimes more effectively, though some victims argue that current laws remain insufficient, particularly regarding cross-border abuse.

Faizan, a young boy from Kashmir, was fatally shot by paramilitary soldiers while returning home near a polling station during a parliamentary by-election marked by violent protests and a historic low voter turnout. Eyewitnesses allege that soldiers fired into the crowd, killing Faizan and seven others, which has led to complaints against the forces and widespread condemnation. The incident occurred amidst a severe boycott by separatist groups and deep political disillusionment, resulting in the lowest voter participation in decades.

A woman has died after being involved in a collision with a silver Ford Transit truck on Nantlle Road in Talysarn, Gwynedd, on Friday afternoon. Although she was flown to Ysbyty Gwynedd by air ambulance, she later passed away. North Wales Police are currently appealing for witnesses to assist with their investigation.

Four transport companies—Abellio, Arriva, KeolisAmey, and MTR—have submitted bids for the next Wales and Borders rail franchise, with the successful operator expected to be selected in early 2018. The Welsh Government’s new "not for profit" model will cap profits, requiring any excess funds to be reinvested into the railway, while also mandating the delivery of the Cardiff Metro upgrade. This marks the first time the Welsh Government has awarded a rail franchise, focusing on improving service quality and passenger numbers across the region.

Robbie Robinson, the 80-year-old broadcaster known for championing the Doric dialect, is stepping down as the permanent host of BBC Scotland’s *Take the Floor* after more than three decades. Widely recognized as one of Scotland’s most familiar voices, Robinson has been honored with an MBE and a place in the Trad Music Awards Hall of Fame for his passionate promotion of traditional Scottish music. While he will continue to contribute to the BBC through occasional broadcasts, he is handing over the regular hosting duties to Gary Innes to take a well-deserved break.

Carlisle manager Steve Coleman has criticized the league's decision to allow his team to play their flooded "home" fixtures at neutral grounds, arguing that it creates an unfair advantage over other clubs. Coleman contends that this arrangement is inequitable because it exempts Carlisle from the travel burdens faced by visiting teams, while his own club has suffered from postponed games without similar flexibility. Although he expresses sympathy for those affected by the flooding, he maintains that the current handling of the situation shifts the rules in a way that is not fair to the rest of the league.

Two supporters who cut themselves off from a stadium tour were discovered during a security sweep at Old Trafford and handed over to police, who decided not to arrest them. Manchester United confirmed that the pair posed no risk to attendees of the Arsenal game, noting they had already passed through standard security checks. This incident follows a similar scare six months ago when a fake explosive device caused the cancellation of a match against Bournemouth.

Accrington Stanley defeated their Lancashire rivals Preston North End 3-2 in a dramatic EFL Cup match that went to extra time. Billy Kee scored the winning goal in the third minute of stoppage time, securing a famous victory for the League Two side against their higher-league opponents. This win marks the second consecutive year Accrington has eliminated higher-division opposition from the competition.

Cardiff handyman Andrew Bickel went viral after a cat charity shop mistakenly returned his stolen tools, leading to a flurry of media attention and interview offers. Bickel, who enjoyed his brief fame, plans to donate any potential earnings from the story to both cat and dog charities. He expressed relief that the mix-up resulted in no financial loss for anyone involved.

Scottish runner Eilidh Muir has confirmed she will miss the Commonwealth Games to focus on completing her final year of veterinary medicine studies. Despite being "gutted" to miss the event, she remains optimistic about her athletic future, potentially targeting the World Indoor Championships in March and multiple upcoming Olympics. Muir recently celebrated a strong performance at the World Athletics Championships, where she set new personal bests in the 1500m and 5,000m events.

Southend United manager Phil Brown expects former Newcastle striker Nile Ranger to return to training before the start of the League One season, despite being jailed for eight months for online banking fraud. Brown indicated that the club plans to arrange closed-door games to help the 26-year-old regain match fitness, although he cautioned that Ranger’s recent absence means he may not be fully prepared for the season opener on 5 August.

Veteran broadcaster Sir Terry Wogan has died of cancer at the age of 77, prompting tributes from colleagues, politicians, and fans across the UK. Condolence books have been opened in his hometown of Limerick and at the BBC’s London headquarters, while figures like Jeremy Clarkson and Prime Minister David Cameron praised his humor, professionalism, and enduring impact on British broadcasting.

Unions at BAE Systems have warned of potential delays to the Royal Navy's Type 26 frigate program, raising fears that up to 800 jobs could be lost if commitments are not met. While Scottish political leaders from the SNP, Labour, and Liberal Democrats expressed deep concern over the uncertainty and called for guaranteed assurances, Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson insisted that the government has confirmed the original timetable and order numbers remain unchanged.

During a heated Republican debate, Donald Trump faced intense criticism from rivals Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz regarding his business record, conservative credentials, and policy details, leading to a chaotic exchange of personal insults. Although the attacks successfully put the front-runner on the defensive, analysts suggest that such late-stage opposition may be too little, too late to stop Trump, who has already won three of the first four contests. The debate highlighted the growing realization among other candidates that Trump is a viable winner, even as they struggle to mount an effective challenge ahead of Super Tuesday.

Ukrainian artist Jamala won the Eurovision Song Contest with her politically charged song "1944," defeating favorites from Russia and Australia in a result that sparked significant debate. While many praised the performance for its emotional depth and historical significance regarding the deportation of Crimean Tatars, critics argued that the victory was driven by its political message against Russia rather than musical quality. The win highlighted the tension between Eurovision's rules against political content and the song's reflection of current geopolitical tensions in the region.

Rother District Council has allocated £51,000 to fund a lifeguard service at Camber Sands in East Sussex following a series of significant and unprecedented drowning deaths. The patrols, which will run from late May to the end of the summer holidays, aim to protect visitors and support the local tourism economy while emphasizing the importance of water safety awareness. The council remains committed to reviewing coroner recommendations as full inquests into the tragedies are awaited.

Partick Thistle players, including captain Osman and Adam Barton, have expressed strong support for manager Alan Archibald, urging him to stay after he was linked with other managerial vacancies. The squad praised Archibald’s consistency and loyalty, noting that his departure would be difficult to replace following his success in guiding the team to a top-six finish. Meanwhile, the club is also on the verge of losing centre-back Liam Lindsay, who has traveled to Barnsley for a medical ahead of a potential transfer.

Canadian police detained ten individuals at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport and confiscated their passports, though no charges have been filed as investigations continue. Public Safety Minister Steven Blaney praised the officers' vigilance in addressing the global terror threat, while the families of the suspects have been informed and are struggling to understand the situation. This incident occurs against the backdrop of Canada's ongoing military involvement in the coalition against IS militants in Iraq and Syria.

Twenty-one-year-old Dixon, who recently made his debut for the Tigers and captained their under-21 side, is set to potentially debut for the Minstermen in Saturday's match against Newport. The Minstermen are currently at the bottom of the Football League.

The UK government aims to save £500 million annually by cracking down on "health tourism" and improving the recovery of costs from foreign visitors, arguing that the current system is too generous. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt stated that these savings would fund 4,000 additional doctors, although critics argue that requiring GPs to vet patient eligibility is impractical. While emergency and infectious disease treatments remain free for all, the government plans to enforce stricter charges on non-European temporary residents to ensure the NHS remains a national service.

Belfast Giants secured a decisive 5-2 victory over the Braehead Clan, with goals from Colin Shields, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano. The win extends Belfast's lead in the standings, giving them a game in hand on their rivals, the Devils. The Giants will continue their busy festive schedule with upcoming matches against Manchester Storm and Braehead Clan.

After undergoing significant restoration, a historic steam engine is set to make its first journey in ten years along the East Coast mainline. Originally built in Doncaster and named after its Edinburgh to London service, the locomotive became a global icon of British engineering after touring the world following the withdrawal of its class in 1966.

One of 249 men suing the Catholic Church over historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school has been awarded £14,000 in compensation, while three other claims were dismissed in the same High Court hearing. The lawsuit follows the imprisonment of former head James Carragher and chaplain Anthony McCallen for multiple sex offenses committed at the now-closed school. The De La Salle Brothers, who ran the school, have issued an unreserved apology for the abuse, with further compensation claims expected later in 2017.
